title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
subtitle: Every agent in my estate reaches every tool through MCP: a gateway of 475 tools, generated servers, a product server ported to .NET, and a single discovery tool backed by a model.

stats.label: work-lifecycle actions across eleven AgentOS tools
actions across 18 FAFO Core tools, dispatch compiled from YAML
tools on the digital-employee server, 13 of them meeting actions

lede: FAFOHive is the single endpoint every managed agent seat in my estate connects to, because I wanted one trust model for every tool an agent can reach. The provider tools sit under stable namespaces, and every provider call is durably accounted, so a restart does not repeat one. See Agents with real tools and no keys. I design tools around jobs: in one module I threw away 83 generated endpoint tools for about fifteen designed ones, a set that later grew to thirty-six. Tool descriptions state their cost and pass the provider's errors through verbatim, so the agent reasons over real failures.
quote: I treat MCP as an engineering surface with identity, cost and failure designed in.
evidence: MCP server design: one endpoint for every managed agent seat serving 475 tools, with provider calls durably accounted so a restart does not repeat one, over a stateless per-request transport.
Agent orchestration over MCP: the AgentOS work lifecycle exposed as about 45 actions across eleven tools, with caller identity derived on the server, idempotency keys and receipts.
Tool-schema context cost reduction: a 41,990-token catalog collapsed into one discovery tool of about 100 tokens, its description capped by a test at 520 characters.
Tool synthesis and governed API integration: about 180 actions across 18 tools compiled from YAML schemas at build time, and a tool that emits new MCP tools.
author: Corey James
